intro.title: Recording Today's Waves
description: We often get swept away by a huge wave called 'anxiety,' without knowing exactly what we're feeling right now.
This wave isn't just one emotion—it's a single wave made of many feelings layered together.
Shall we take a moment to discover which emotions make up the waves rolling toward you?
intro.contentDescription: A practice of breaking down vague anxiety into specific emotions to face the true feelings within.
steps: 1. Situation (Fact): When, where, and what happened?
2. Thought (Thought): What thoughts crossed your mind at that moment?
3. Emotion (Emotion): What emotions did those thoughts bring?
intro.tip: Tip: 'Thoughts' are just wind with no substance. The key is discovering how you interpreted the situation.

step1.question: What happened?
step1.description: Write down the facts of the moment that shook your ocean—objectively, as if a camera were recording it.
step1.exampleBad: X: I felt pathetic because I was lazy and didn't study at all.
step1.exampleGood: I planned to study for 3 hours today, but ended up spending all 3 hours on my phone.

step2.question: What thoughts crossed your mind?
step2.description: Write down the interpretations or thoughts that brushed across your surface, layered on top of the facts.
step2.exampleBad: X: I felt defeated and didn't want to study anymore. (This is an emotion.)
step2.exampleGood: I thought, "I have no willpower," and "What if I fail the exam because of this?"

step3.question: What emotions did you feel?
step3.description: Find the true identity of the wave or any physical sensations those thoughts brought.

step.placeholder: Freely write down the emotions you felt at the time.

result.title: You've found the true emotions within the wave
description: This wave is no longer a mysterious, overwhelming anxiety.
The moment you gave it a name, the wave became a 'specific feeling' you can face and embrace.
Shall we move to the next step and observe this wave as it is, without trying to suppress it?
